entry.title: CS5489 Home Assignment 4
entry.content:
Due on November 20, 2026, 11:59pm

Exercise 1

[2 points]. Prove that the eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix $A \in R^{N ×N}$ ,
where $A = A^\top$ , are real-valued (i.e., not complex-valued). Prove also that
the eigenvectors of A corresponding to different eigenvalues are orthogonal
to each other

Proof.

For $v,\ w \in \mathbb C^N$, let $\langle v, w \rangle$ denote $v^\top \bar w$ , where $\bar w$ is the complex conjugate of the vector $w$.

Let $t \in \mathbb C$. Then

$$\begin{equation} \bar t \langle v,\ w\rangle = \bar t v^\top \bar w = v^\top \bar t \bar w = v^\top \overline{t w} = \langle v,\ tw\rangle \end{equation}.$$

$$\begin{equation} t\langle v,\ w \rangle = tv^\top \bar w= (tv)^\top \overline w = \langle tv,\ w \rangle \end{equation}$$

$$\begin{equation} \langle v,\ v \rangle = v^\top \bar v= v_1 \overline v_1 + \ldots + v_N \overline v_N \geq 0\end{equation}$$

where $v = (v_1, \ \ldots ,\ v_N)^\top$.
Let $A^*$ denote the complex transpose of a matrix $A$. Then
$$\langle v, Av \rangle = v^\top \overline{Av}=v^\top \overline{A^\top}^\top v=v^\top (A^*)^\top v = (A^* v)^\top v = \langle A^* v ,\ v \rangle$$
Suppose $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ associated with the eigenvalue $\lambda$.

If $\langle v,\ v\rangle = 0$, then $v_1 \overline v_1 + \ldots + v_N \overline v_N =0$. Since $v_i \overline v_i \geq 0$ and $=0$ only when $v_i=0$, we know

$$v_i=0 \quad {\rm for \ each\ } i \in \{1,\ldots,N\}.$$
Hence $v=0$. In this case, the eigenvalue of $v$ is $0$, which is real valued.

If $\langle v,\ v\rangle >0$, then

$$\overline\lambda = \frac{1}{\langle v,\ v\rangle}\overline \lambda \langle v,\ v\rangle$$

By Eq $\boxed{\overline t\langle v,\ w \rangle=\langle v,\ tw \rangle}$, we get
$$\overline \lambda =\frac{1}{\langle v,\ v\rangle} \langle v,\ \lambda v\rangle =\frac{1}{\langle v,\ v\rangle} \langle v,\ Av \rangle$$
By $\boxed {\langle v, Av \rangle = \langle A^* v ,\ v \rangle}$, we get
$$\overline \lambda = \frac{1}{\langle v,\ v\rangle} \langle A^* v ,\ v \rangle=\frac{1}{\langle v,\ v\rangle} \langle \lambda v,\ v\rangle = \frac{1}{\langle v,\ v\rangle} \lambda \langle v,\ v\rangle = \lambda$$

So we have derived that $\boxed{\overline \lambda = \lambda}$. So any eigenvalue of $A$ is real-valued.

Suppose $v,\ w$ are eigenvectors of $A$ associated with $\lambda_v$ and $\lambda_w$. Then

$$\langle Av,\ w \rangle = \lambda_v \langle v,\ w \rangle$$
and since $A\in \mathbb R^{N\times N}$,
$$\langle Av,\ w \rangle = \langle v,\ A^*w \rangle = \langle v,\ A^\top w \rangle=\langle v,\ Aw \rangle = \lambda_w \langle v,\ w \rangle.$$

So
$$0 =\langle Av,\ w \rangle - \langle Av,\ w \rangle = (\lambda_v - \lambda_w) \langle v,\ w \rangle$$
which implies $\langle v,\ w \rangle = 0$ because $\lambda_v - \lambda_w \neq 0$.

  • I computed matrix of the adjoin operator $T^*$ under an orthonormal matrix, showing that it is the transpose matrix of $T$ under the same basis when they are over $\mathbb R$ .
  • The adjoin operator of the restriction of an operator can be computed, too, via projection.

      • How is the projection operator used? Did it simplify the calculation?
        logseq.order-list-type:: number
        • It computed the projection of $A^t \alpha$ unto $V$. No.

2026-11-12: I just revisited this question. do not know what it says or the solution itself.
Then i seem to realize what it means.
$L_A \alpha - A^t \alpha$ is orthogonal to $\beta_1,\,\beta_2$.
So, it is in the space $V^\top$ spanned by the vector orthogonal to both $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ .
A spanning vector of $V^\top$ is $(1 \quad -1\quad 0)^\top$.
Let $v = (1 \quad -1 \quad 0)^\top$ and $v_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} (1 \quad -1 \quad 0)^\top$ is its normalization.

$$\begin{align*} & (1 \quad 3 \quad -1)\ v_n \cdot v_n \\ =\ & \frac{1}{2}\ (1 \quad 3 \quad -1)\ \begin{pmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \\ =\ & \frac{1}{2} \times 2\ \begin{pmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \\ =\ & \begin{pmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \end{align*}$$

So the answer is

$$\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \fbox {$\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$}.$$

entry.title: Perceptron
entry.content:
为什么w 更新是加，$\theta$ 更新是减

以 ADALINE 为例，$y= w^Tx -\theta$，$E=\tfrac12(z-y)^2$，$\Delta=-\eta\,\partial E/\partial(\cdot)$：

$$\frac{\partial E}{\partial w_i}=\underbrace{\frac{\partial E}{\partial y}}_{-(z-y)}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}}_{1}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\partial u}{\partial w_i}}_{x_i}=-(z-y)x_i \quad\Rightarrow\quad \Delta w_i=+\eta(z-y)x_i$$

$$\frac{\partial E}{\partial \theta}=\underbrace{-(z-y)}_{\partial E/\partial y}\cdot\underbrace{(-1)}_{\partial u/\partial\theta}=+(z-y) \quad\Rightarrow\quad \Delta\theta=-\eta(z-y)$$

θ 就是一个"输入恒为 −1 的权重" delta = lr * (z-y) * input

XOR 不能被单层网络划分

在 $\mathbb R^n$ 里都成立：超平面 $H=\{x: w^{\mathsf T}x+\theta=0\}$（要求 $w\neq0$）把空间分成的两个闭半空间

$$H^{+}=\{x: w^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\ge 0\},\qquad H^{-}=\{x: w^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\le 0\}$$

都是凸集。（$\mathbb R^2$ 里超平面是直线，$\mathbb R^3$ 里是平面。）
注：这里按你的写法 $w^{\mathsf T}x+\theta=0$；本课程 slides 用 $u=\sum w_ix_i-\theta$，只是 θ 符号相反，不影响结论。
证明
凸集定义：$S$ 凸 $\iff$ $\forall x_1,x_2\in S,\ \forall\lambda\in[0,1]$，都有 $\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2\in S$。
第 1 步：仿射函数保持凸组合（关键引理）
令 $f(x)=w^{\mathsf T}x+\theta$，则对任意 $x_1,x_2$ 和 $\lambda\in[0,1]$：
$$f\big(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2\big) = w^{\mathsf T}\big(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2\big)+\theta$$

$$= \lambda w^{\mathsf T}x_1+(1-\lambda)w^{\mathsf T}x_2+\underbrace{\lambda\theta+(1-\lambda)\theta}_{=\ \theta\ (\text{因为 }\lambda+(1-\lambda)=1)} = \lambda f(x_1)+(1-\lambda)f(x_2)$$

（注意最后一步用了 $\lambda+(1-\lambda)=1$——这正是"仿射"（线性 + 常数）而非纯线性的地方。）
第 2 步：半空间的定义立即给出凸性
设 $x_1,x_2\in H^{+}$，即 $f(x_1)\ge0,\ f(x_2)\ge0$。因为 $\lambda\ge0$、$(1-\lambda)\ge0$：
$$f\big(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2\big)=\lambda f(x_1)+(1-\lambda)f(x_2)\ \ge\ \lambda\cdot 0+(1-\lambda)\cdot 0=0$$

所以线段上任一点仍属于 $H^{+}$ ⟹ $H^{+}$ 凸。$H^{-}$ 把不等号反向，同理。$\blacksquare$
三个补充

  1. 等价证法（更"现代"的写法）
    $f$ 是仿射函数 ⟹ 既是凸函数也是凹函数 ⟹ $H^{+}=\{f\le -\theta'\}$… 即 凸函数的下水平集必为凸集，一行证完。（半空间 = 凸函数的 sublevel set。）
  2. 边界与划分的细节
    严格半空间 $\{f>0\}$、$\{f<0\}$ 也是凸的（开集）；
    边界 $\{f=0\}$ 本身是仿射子空间（维度 $n-1$），也凸，但内部为空；
    真正的"划分"是三分：$\{f>0\}\ \dot\cup\ \{f=0\}\ \dot\cup\ \{f<0\}$；两个闭半空间在边界上重叠。
    退化情形：若 $w=0$，则 $\theta=0$ 时 $H^+=H^-=\mathbb R^n$（没切开），$\theta\neq0$ 时一半为空——所以定理要求 $w\neq0$。
  3. 为什么这个凸性在课程里很重要
    XOR 的本质：单个超平面只能切出凸的（半空间型）区域，而 XOR 的每个类区域是两个不连通的象限（非凸）⟹ 必然切不开。这也是 Q1(b) 那问"用凸包重叠解释"的理论根据：存在分隔超平面 ⟺ 两类点集的凸包不相交（超平面分离定理）。
    SVM 的根基：约束 $y_i(w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b)\ge1$ 是一族半空间，半空间的交仍是凸集 ⟹ SVM 原始问题的可行域是凸多面体，目标 $\tfrac12\lVert w\rVert^2$ 是凸函数 ⟹ 整个原始问题是凸二次规划，有唯一全局最优（KKT 即为充要条件）——Q4(a)(b) 全部建立在这个性质上。

Q1（Midterm，共 10 分）
设一维数据 $\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}$ i.i.d. 来自高斯分布 $\mathcal{N}(x\mid \mu,\sigma^2)$，其中 $\sigma^2$ 已知。
(a) 求 $\mu$ 的最大似然估计 $\hat{\mu}_{ML}$，写出完整推导。（3 分）
(b) 现对 $\mu$ 施加高斯先验 $p(\mu)=\mathcal{N}(\mu\mid m,s^2)$，求 $\mu$ 的 MAP 估计 $\hat{\mu}_{MAP}$。（3 分）
(c) 令 $s^2\to 0$（先验越来越尖锐），$\hat{\mu}_{MAP}$ 趋向什么？请给出解释，并说明这体现了贝叶斯估计与 MLE 的什么关系。（2 分）
(d) 若改用全贝叶斯方法对新样本 $x_*$ 做预测，写出 predictive distribution $p(x_*\mid \mathcal{D})$ 的形式（用共轭性），并说明它与直接用 $\hat{\mu}_{MAP}$ 代入 $\mathcal{N}(x_*\mid\mu,\sigma^2)$ 得到的分布有何区别。（2 分）

entry.title: gossip problem
entry.content:
假设最小反例的存在。那么不可能有重复自己的item到自己。因为这样会给出更小的反例。（正常的情况允许自己到自己）

电话不可能重复。最后一次和第一次的电话ab对a,b都是最后一次/第一次。
所以，不可能开始和最后一次和同一个人打电话。即第一次和最后一次肯定和不同的人打了电话。

例 12,34, 23,41

有多少个电话是最后/开始的？

  • 在上面的例子中，12, 34 都是首次。23, 41 都是最后电话。
    可以看出，前两个中四个人用两次完成了。
    后两个中同样是，四个人用两次，每次两个人同时，完成了最后电话。

中间的电话

不是开始/最后的电话，叫做中间电话。

全体 n 个don当成节点，组成一个图。每个电话是一个边；没参与的人就是孤立点，自己算一个连通分支。

特殊地，在证明的前提内"0 条中间 call"是可能的，那就是 n=5（n−5 = 0）：H 是 5 个孤立点 = 恰好 5 个分支，"at least five" 正好取等。这一情形随后被 p(a) ≥ 5 排掉。

如果b 从a 传播信息，那么b 在a 的联通分量中。
如果 b 向a 传播信息，那么b在c的联通分量中，这里 c是最后一个a的通话对象。

所以，至少有5-2=3 个连通分量，既没有来自a的信息，也没有向a传递信息。
对这些分量中的边，对a而言v是无用的。
这些分量中的边数$\le$ 对a而言无用的电话。

先区分“传递来自a信息”和“向a传递信息”两种电话。

在 AB, CD, AC, BD（k=4，取 a=A）里，标记两个方向：
通话 from A（传 item A） to A（信息流向 A）
1 AB ✓（B 第一次知道 A） ✓（B 的 item 立刻到 A）
2 CD ✗ ✓（D 经后面 AC 到 A）
3 AC ✓（C 第一次知道 A） ✓（C、D 的 item 到 A）
4 BD ✓（D 第一次知道 A） ✗（之后没有通话能到达 A）
所以

  • F = {AB, AC, BD}
  • T = {AB, CD, AC}
  • F∩T = {AB, AC}
    即 a=A 亲自打的那两通，正好都同时属于两个方向；而 p(A)=2，所以 |F∩T| = 2 = p(A)（满足 |F∩T| ≤ p(a)）。
    顺带验算一下这条式子：k=4，|F|=n−1=3，|T|=3，|F∩T|=2，w(a)=0（无浪费通话），
    4 ≥ 3 + 3 − 2 + 0 = 4 ✓
    这里取等号，因为它是可行的最优方案（k=2n−4），不是书中那个假想的 k=2n−5 反例。

nohoi 导致，只有a本人参与的电话，才有可能同时符合两种。（为什么？）
所以：# “传递来自a信息”$\cap$ #“向a传递信息” $\le$ # a 本人打的电话

entry.content:
DP 需要把大的问题归结到小的问题。但是「大小」的定义取决于具体的问题。

在背包问题中，比较明显——大小是包的总重量。

在SPP中，是「最多」允许的步数$k$. 当$k$ 小的时候，很多路径不存在，最小距离简单地变成$\infty$ . 接下来，我们可以对下一个更大的$k+1$ 步内的解进行寻找。

entry.title: lang stat
entry.content:
The plan of lang stat project.

Follow methods in https://allendowney.github.io/ThinkBayes2/

Initialization

Find a suitable data of language text and download it. Suitable for unsupervised data analysis, such as cluster etc.

Problems

What are noticable features in the language corpus?

How to ask good stat questions (Key Principles & Rules)

At its core, asking a good statistical question means translating real-world uncertainty or business needs into a measurable, testable, and decision-driven statistical proposition. If the question itself is vague or biased, even the most advanced machine learning models or statistical tests will fail—a classic case of "Garbage in, garbage out."

When formulating a statistical question, follow these 6 essential rules:

Rule 1: Make it Specific & Measurable

Avoid subjective, vague, or loose terms (such as "good," "much," or "significantly improved"). Define clear, quantitative metrics instead.

  • Poor Question: "Is our new landing page doing well?"

  • Good Question: "Over the 14 days following release, did the new landing page yield a statistically significant increase ($\ge 2\%$) in daily paid conversion rates among users aged 25–34 compared to the old page?"

Rule 2: Clearly Define the Population & Sample Scope

Statistical inferences apply only to the specific population under study. Explicitly define the target audience, timeframe, and geographical or platform bounds to avoid overgeneralization.

  • Poor Question: "Which recommendation algorithm do users prefer?"

  • Good Question: "Among active iOS mobile users over the past 30 days, does Algorithm A achieve a higher mean 1-day retention rate than Algorithm B?"

Rule 3: Remain Unbiased & Neutral

A well-formulated statistical question must not presuppose an answer or lead the data toward a specific conclusion.

  • Poor Question: "Why are most users satisfied with our new feature?" (Presupposes widespread satisfaction)

  • Good Question: "What is the distribution and median of overall satisfaction scores among a random sample of 1,000 users who tried the new feature?"

Rule 4: Ensure Testability & Falsifiability

A statistical question should translate into formal null ($H_0$) and alternative ($H_1$) hypotheses that can be rejected or failed to be rejected based on observed data.

  • Poor Question: "Is product quality the fundamental driver of sales volume?" (Too broad and difficult to isolate)

  • Good Question: "After controlling for ad spend and seasonality, is there a statistically significant negative correlation ($p < 0.05$) between product return rates (a proxy for quality) and repeat purchase rates?"

Rule 5: Distinguish Association from Causation

Clarify whether you are asking a descriptive question, looking for a statistical association, or attempting to establish a causal relationship. Causal questions require controlled experimental designs (e.g., A/B testing).

  • Association: "Is daily active time positively correlated with total monthly spend?"

  • Causation: "Does issuing a $5 discount coupon (treatment) cause a statistically significant increase in average 30-day spending compared to the control group?"

Rule 6: Aim for Practical Significance & Actionability

Statistical significance ($p < 0.05$) does not always translate to practical business significance. The answer to a good statistical question should directly inform a specific decision or action.

  • Poor Question: "Is the 0.001-second difference in click response time between Group A and Group B statistically significant?" (Technically testable, but practically meaningless)

  • Good Question: "Does reducing page load time by 500ms using the new compression algorithm increase conversion rates by at least 0.5% with statistical significance?"

Checklist for Evaluation

Before finalizing your statistical question, evaluate it against this checklist:

Dimension Self-Check Question
Metrics Are the independent (input) and dependent (output) variables clearly defined?
Population Are the boundaries (time, user segment, platform) explicitly stated?
Testability Can this be proved or disproved using a hypothesis test or mathematical model?
Feasibility Do you have access to sufficient data and sample size to answer the question?
Actionability Will the outcome (reject or fail to reject $H_0$) trigger a clear next action?

Building

Implement the code while leaving a few essential blanks for the user to fill, for the educational purpose.

Designing code completion exercises (fill-in-the-blank code) for statistics requires balancing pedagogical focus, syntax constraints, and statistical comprehension. The goal is to test whether students understand the statistical concept and API logic, not whether they can guess arbitrary variable names.

Below are the core rules and strategies for creating effective fill-in-the-blank statistics exercises.

Core Rules for Designing Blank Spaces

Rule 1: Target Statistical Logic, Not Boilerplate

Leave blanks where students must demonstrate understanding of statistical concepts (e.g., choosing the correct distribution function, formula, parameter, or evaluation metric). Keep setup, data loading, and syntax boilerplate intact.

  • Poor: import _____ as pd (Tests basic Python syntax, not statistics)

  • Better: ttest_ind(group_a, group_b, alternative='_____') (Tests hypothesis directionality)

Rule 2: Ensure Unambiguous Answers

A blank should ideally have one canonical correct answer (or a very narrow set of equivalents). Avoid blanks where multiple valid approaches could fit unless your grading system explicitly supports regular expressions or AST parsing.

  • Ambiguous: df['height'].____() (Could be .mean(), .median(), .std(), etc.)

  • Unambiguous: # Compute the 95th percentile $\rightarrow$ np.percentile(df['height'], ____)

Rule 3: Maintain Code Structure & Executability

The surrounding code should remain syntactically valid around the blank. Use consistent placeholder notation that indicates what type of input is expected.

  • Standard Placeholders:

    • ___ (three underscores) for general code gaps.

    • /* YOUR CODE HERE */ for multi-character or expression-level gaps.

    • None or ... (Ellipsis in Python) if the code needs to remain syntactically valid before student edits.

Key Categories of Statistical Blanks (With Examples)

1. Statistical Distributions & Parameters

Test whether students understand which distribution function to use (pdf/pmf, cdf, or ppf/qnorm) and how parameters map to theoretical concepts.

  • R Example (Normal Distribution Quantiles):

    R

    # Find the z-score corresponding to the 97.5th percentile of N(0,1)
z_crit <- qnorm(p = ____, mean = 0, sd = 1)

  • Python Example (Binomial PMF):

    Python

    from scipy.stats import binom
# Probability of getting exactly 5 heads in 10 fair coin flips
prob = binom.pmf(k=5, n=10, p=____)

2. Hypothesis Testing & Decisions

Focus on test selection, hypothesis directionality (alternative), or decision rules based on $\alpha$ and $p$-values.

  • Python Example (T-Test Directionality):

    Python

    # Test if Group A mean is significantly GREATER than Group B
stat, p_val = ttest_ind(group_a, group_b, alternative='____')

  • R Example (Decision Rule):

    R

    alpha <- 0.05
# Reject Null Hypothesis if p-value is below significance level
if (p_val ____ alpha) {
  print("Reject H0")
}

3. Formula Specifications in Modeling

In regression models, leave blanks for formula design (e.g., interaction terms, log transformations, or random effects).

  • R Example (Linear Model with Interaction):

    R

    # Fit a model predicting yield using temp, fertilizer, and their interaction
model <- lm(yield ~ temp ____ fertilizer, data = crop_data)

4. Data Transformation & Filtering

Target key statistical operations like standardizing ($Z$-score conversion), grouping, or pivoting.

  • Python Example (Standardization):

    Python

    # Standardize variable X: (X - mean) / std
z_scores = (df['X'] - df['X'].mean()) / df['X'].____()

Best Practices for Scaffolding & Grading

  1. Provide Clear Context via Comments: State the statistical goal directly above the code block. Do not force students to reverse-engineer the prompt from incomplete syntax.

  2. One Concept Per Line: Avoid putting multiple blanks on a single line unless testing a closely coupled concept (e.g., mean and sd together).

  3. Use Expected Output Annotations: Include expected output or assertion tests directly below the exercise so students can self-check:

    Python

    mean_val = df['age'].____()
# Assert for automated autograding environments
assert np.isclose(mean_val, 34.25), "Check your calculation method!"

Summary Checklist for Instructors

Criterion Check
Focus Does the blank test a statistical concept rather than general programming syntax?
Uniqueness Is there a single, unambiguous correct answer for the blank?
Clarity Is the prompt comment explicit about what value/function is required?
Scaffold Is all necessary data preprocessing provided prior to the blank?
Validation Is there an automated check or expected output provided for student feedback?

后验分布

参数$\theta$ 的后验分布的密度是 $P(\theta |D)$。 这个是参数的分布

$$P(\theta |D ) = \frac{P(D \mid \theta) P(\theta)}{P(D)}$$

$P(D)$ 的定义是样本密度。类似于 Class Notes 中的“平均有多少个样本落在类别 c 中”。

后验预测 $P(x^\star \mid \theta )$

这只是给定参数$\theta$ 的$x$. （意思是 $P(X = x^\star \mid \theta)$ , $X$ 有一个参数是$\theta$. 的分布）

后验估计:

$$p(x^\star | D) = \int P(x^\star \mid \theta)P(\theta |D)d\theta$$

  • prior 的初始参数怎么选都可以吗？

MAP 和后验分布区别

后验分布是一个分布。MAP 是求出一个参数的数字。

Example: 可以算这个 $y$ 的后验分布

SVM

Why should we penalize the weight ？

# step size for the sliding window
step = 4

# extract window patches with step size of 4
patches = skimage.util.view_as_windows(testimg, (19,19), step=step)
psize = patches.shape

# collapse the first 2 dimensions
patches2 = patches.reshape((psize[0]*psize[1], psize[2], psize[3]))
print(patches2.shape )

# histogram equalize patches (improves contrast)
patches3 = empty(patches2.shape)
for i in range(patches2.shape[0]):
    patches3[i,:,:] = skimage.exposure.equalize_hist(patches2[i,:,:])

# extract features
newXf = extract_features(patches3)

view_as_windows extract 图像，通过滑动窗口。大小19$\times$ 19
pateches.shape 「原本」的形状
patches.reshape 重新塑形。 （应该是自动判断前两个怎么collapse？）
每个 patches2[i,:,:] 是一个小patch.
patches2 第一个维度是什么：是所有patch 的数量

patches 前两个维度是什么？num_y_win (y方向窗口数量) 和 num_x_win (x方向窗口数量)。
num_y_win 窗口上下滑动一共能产生多少行窗口
num_x_win 窗口左右滑动一共能产生多少行窗口

后验分布

Maximum a posterior

如果在$\theta=t$ 时，数据$D$ 有分布$p(D|\theta =t)$. 并且我们也假设知道$\theta$ 是什么分布。那么MAP 就是计算

$$\arg \max_\theta p(\theta = t|D=x) = \arg \max_\theta \frac{p(D=x \mid \theta =t)p(\theta =t)}{\displaystyle\sum_s p(D=x|\theta=s)}$$

[修改] 实际上 分母和$\theta$ 没关系，所以只要最大化分子就可以

$$\arg \max_\theta p(\theta = t|D=x) = \arg \max_\theta p(D=x \mid \theta =t)p(\theta =t)$$

ML是反过来P 中 的 $\theta$ 和$D$

Posterior Estimation

用全部后验分布的全部概率产生的结果加权平均（？）

Bernoulli Update

一开始的先验是关于参数$\pi$ 的beta分布。
结果是一个伯努利分布中参数 $\pi$ 的分布。

K-means

$\pi_k$ 观察到第k堆的概率。这是一个隐变量 $Z= k$ 的概率。

观察到向量$x_i$ 的条件下，在第$k$ 堆的概率：

$$\gamma_{ik} = P(Z= k\mid x_i )$$

因为一个空间所有样本概率总和为$1$, 所以
$$\sum_k \gamma_{ik} = 1. \tag{1}$$

K means - Soft Assignment

$Z = k \mid x_i$ 不是一个常数(即，不在任意一点概率是1)。

$Z \sim N(\mu_k^{(0)}, \sigma_k^{(0)})$ 时
E-M step 可以更新$\mu_k$ 和$\sigma_k$. 分别有一个公式……

Hard Assignment

$\gamma_{ik} \in \{0,\ 1\}$ 。更新后的中心是一堆中所有点的平均

$$\mu_{k}^{(1)}=\frac{\sum \gamma_{ik} x_i}{\sum_i\gamma_{ik}} =\frac{\sum_{i在第k堆中} x_i}{\sum_{i 在第k堆中} 1}$$

MLE 和 MAP 区别

1. 极大似然估计（MLE）

  • 不需要先验（No Prior）。
  • 基本逻辑：只关注当前观察到的数据 $x$。它假设参数 $\theta$ 是一个固定但未知的真实常数，寻找能使数据 $x$ 出现概率（似然 $p(x \mid \theta)$）最大的那个 $\theta$。
  • 数学表示：
    $$\hat{\theta}_{\text{MLE}} = \arg\max_{\theta} p(x \mid \theta)$$

2. 后验估计（例如 最大后验估计 MAP）

  • 必须需要先验（Requires Prior）。
  • 基本逻辑：基于贝叶斯学派的观点，参数 $\theta$ 本身也是一个随机变量，在观察到数据之前我们就对它有一定的认知或倾向（先验分布 $p(\theta)$）。后验估计通过贝叶斯公式将“先验”与“数据似然”结合，寻找使后验概率 $p(\theta \mid x)$ 最大的 $\theta$。
  • 数学表示：
    $$\hat{\theta}_{\text{MAP}} = \arg\max_{\theta} p(\theta \mid x) = \arg\max_{\theta} \left[ \underbrace{p(x \mid \theta)}_{\text{似然}} \cdot \underbrace{p(\theta)}_{\text{先验}} \right]$$

总结对比

  • MLE = 纯粹看数据（$\text{数据似然}$）
  • 后验估计（MAP） = 数据 + 经验（$\text{数据似然} \times \text{先验概率}$）
    当先验分布 $p(\theta)$ 是均匀分布（即对所有可能的 $\theta$ 不偏不倚，等概率看待）时，MAP 的计算结果就会退化为与 MLE 完全一致。

Full Posterior distribution vs. MAP

class 1 with probability $p$
class 2 with probability $1-p$
The ratio is $\frac{p}{1 - p}$.
if both in the form exp, then $\log p/(1-p) = \log (exp (\cdot)) = \cdot$


不太明白：求出来likelihood ，但是不知道参数是什么。用MLE 来计算吗？
